bindings.label: A 2-month-old male infant presented with a progressively enlarging purplish-red mass in the right lower limb since birth.

The mass measured approximately 5 × 5 cm with purplish-red discoloration and surrounding tissue swelling; physical examination revealed a 5 × 5 cm mass at the right knee joint that was warm to touch, of medium consistency, and well-defined; hemorrhagic spots were noted on the upper hard palate.

Past medical history, personal history, and immunization status were normal; there were no postnatal episodes of cyanosis, convulsions, or bleeding; family history was negative for congenital malformations, tumors, or hemorrhagic conditions.
Vital signs were stable, the infant was alert, and no abnormalities were detected in the central nervous, cardiovascular, or respiratory systems.
Laboratory tests show platelet count 18 × 10^9/L and fibrinogen 0.541 g/L
PT/APTT/TT are prolonged and D-dimer is 21.29
MRI shows an enhancing right inguinal/thigh mass with mixed enhancement
Biopsy with immunohistochemistry for the vascular mass has not yet been performed
Serial platelet and fibrinogen trend data are not yet available
